mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, which drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate below 4% for two consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing corporate margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) of more than 2% coincident with a decline in housing starts (HOUST) signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces revenue growth for cyclicals and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS YoY < -2% AND HOUST declines for 2 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for three consecutive months signals a contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces earnings for industrial firms and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) above their 12-month moving averages signals a broad-based demand recovery, which boosts earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained period (six months) where the CPI inflation index (CPIAUCSL) exceeds the FEDFUNDS rate by more than 2 percentage points signals real negative interest rates, which incentivizes risk-taking and boosts equity valuations, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) of more than 200,000 in two consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which supports corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent quarterly decline in real GDP (GDPC1) of more than 1.5% signals a broad-based demand contraction, which reduces corporate revenues and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days, except during periods of aggressive monetary easing.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes when FEDFUNDS is not in easing mode.
